clue.text: Having won holiday, I missed out, in total disarray

indicators.note: something missed is left behind, so the single letter named just before it drops out of the fodder
letters that are out of place have been knocked out of order, so the remaining fodder is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letter that is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone wins a holiday but misses the trip and is left in a complete muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of WON HOLIDAY and rearrange the nine letters left to get ANY OLD HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase describes something done carelessly, without order or method, much like a messy jumble.

clue.text: A grave situation - order second category weapon

blocks.note: taken as written
a tomb is the place where a burial is situated
the Order of Merit, a British honour
B is the second grade after A

explanation.surface: A dire state of affairs calls for a second-rate weapon to be ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour that crosswords often use for 'order'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear fission bomb is a devastating explosive device used in war, so it is a kind of armament.

clue.text: Some betrayal tactically here during WWII?

indicators.note: only some of the following words are used, so the letters sit inside the run of the clue

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A question hinting at some wartime treachery planned at a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the 1945 Allied conference took place at this Crimean resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin met in this Crimean resort in February 1945 to plan the postwar settlement.

clue.text: When AA members need clarification of a way forward?

definitions.text: When AA members need clarification of a way forward?

blocks.clueFragment: When AA members need clarification of a way forward?
blocks.note: surface reading: the moment recovering drinkers want guidance on how to proceed

blocks.clueFragment: When AA members need clarification of a way forward?
blocks.note: setter's reading: AA is the Automobile Association, so its members are motorists who need headlamps to see the road ahead

explanation.surface: When people in Alcoholics Anonymous want guidance on the path ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: AA suggests Alcoholics Anonymous, but here it is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation; the clarification is literal light on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The official period after dusk when vehicles must switch on their lamps, which is when motorists need to see the road.

clue.text: Jack's crying out for the sack!

blocks.note: first meaning: the sailors' chant when hauling ropes together, a jack being a sailor
second meaning: dismissal, as in giving someone their marching orders

explanation.surface: A sailor is shouting out, desperate to be fired from his job.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (as in jack tar) is a crossword sailor; the second meaning comes from the phrase 'give someone the heave-ho'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the rhythmic shout of seamen pulling together, and informally a dismissal from a job or relationship.

clue.text: Part of building rented, one with restricted lift facility

blocks.note: a wing is a section projecting from a main building
property that is let has been rented out

explanation.surface: A section of a building has been rented out and has only a limited elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lift facility' sounds like an elevator, but it is aerodynamic lift: a small wing gives only limited lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wing or wingtip extension on an aircraft generates only a modest amount of upward aerodynamic force.

clue.text: Assistance required for Beatles' performance

blocks.note: first meaning: aid given to someone
second meaning: the title of a 1965 Beatles song and film

explanation.surface: Someone needs support to stage a Beatles show.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday word for aid or support is also the exclamation-marked title of a famous Beatles single and film.

clue.text: Mutually excited and explosive in race riot?

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so all the gathered letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: someone hot is aroused or worked up
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two sides are equally inflamed and volatile during a race riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutually' is an adverb and the answer a pronoun phrase, but they swap in sentences such as 'they help mutually / they help each other'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mutually means two parties do it reciprocally, one to the other, in both directions.

clue.text: Show off these days, staying in trim

indicators.note: one thing staying in another is lodged inside it, so the short piece goes within the longer word

blocks.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
to pare is to trim or cut back

explanation.surface: Nowadays people flaunt themselves while keeping in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: AD, anno domini, covers the current era, so it stands for 'these days'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt or display something ostentatiously is to put it on public display, as a procession does.

clue.text: Tip for drivers? It may affect one's own behaviour

definitions.text: It may affect one's own behaviour

blocks.note: first meaning, read whimsically: a piece of advice for motorists, auto being a car

blocks.clueFragment: It may affect one's own behaviour
blocks.note: second meaning: the psychological process of influencing oneself

explanation.surface: Advice for motorists that might change how they conduct themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the word as a car plus a hint, which is why it carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology, it is the process by which a person unconsciously influences their own beliefs, feelings or conduct.

clue.text: Prison officers occupied old fellow - one always inside

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for fellow
an old lag is a habitual convict, forever back in jail

explanation.surface: Guards took over a jail for an old fellow who is always locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison officers' suggests warders, but it means a prison for officers. An old lag is British slang for a hardened, repeat prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: German prisoner-of-war camps for captured commissioned military men were called this, short for Offizierslager.

clue.text: One presiding over award ceremony for the MC?

definitions.text: One presiding over award ceremony for the MC?

blocks.clueFragment: One presiding over award ceremony for the MC?
blocks.note: surface reading: the official handing out a Military Cross at a medal parade

blocks.clueFragment: One presiding over award ceremony for the MC?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the MC is a master of ceremonies, and this person reads out the winners at a prize event

explanation.surface: Who presides when someone is decorated with the Military Cross?
explanation.walkthrough: MC looks like the Military Cross, a British gallantry medal; read as master of ceremonies it describes the person introducing the awards.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter who introduces acts and reads out the winners at a show or broadcast does the job of a compere.

clue.text: Insect buzzing around wine - a funny little creature

indicators.note: an insect buzzing around something circles it, so its letters enclose the drink

blocks.note: a bee is a familiar insect
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A bug hovers round a glass of wine, an odd little critter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish word is affectionate, familiar from Burns's poem 'To a Mouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scots diminutive denotes a small animal or bug, often used playfully, so it suits an amusing tiny beast.

clue.text: Holy Roman Emperor, given sign, got votes from 11

indicators.note: 11 across is a person who speaks to an audience, so the words come to us as heard, not written

blocks.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a candidate who got votes polled them

explanation.surface: An emperor, handed a star sign, received votes from a presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 11 across, ANNOUNCER, tells you to hear the word as spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Habsburg rulers of this name, Leopold I and Leopold II, held the imperial title of the Holy Roman Empire.

clue.text: Honesty's importance in a crisis?

blocks.note: something of great moment has great significance
the possessive ending turns into 'of' when the words are reordered
truth and honesty are synonyms

explanation.surface: How much honesty matters when things go badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: X's Y becomes the Y of X: honesty's importance is the moment (importance) of truth (honesty).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a decisive turning point when a person or plan is truly tested, which is what a crisis is.

clue.text: He must be involved with the media!

definitions.text: He must be involved with the media!

blocks.clueFragment: He must be involved with the media!
blocks.note: surface reading: a man whose work is bound up with the press and broadcasting

blocks.clueFragment: He must be involved with the media!
blocks.note: setter's reading: media are mediums or middle ways, so this go-between is a man of the middle

explanation.surface: A man whose job ties him to newspapers and television.
explanation.walkthrough: The media suggests journalism, but medium means a middle course, and the go-between stands in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader or agent standing between producer and buyer is an intermediary who arranges deals between two parties.

clue.text: Be intimidating, editing copy thus?

indicators.note: editing text changes it around, so the letters of the words that follow are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Would revising a piece of copy this way frighten someone?
explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase means to unnerve someone, so 'be intimidating' must be read as 'to intimidate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or daunt an opponent through mental pressure is to undermine their confidence, a form of intimidation.

clue.text: Finally, they just miss a century

definitions.text: Finally, they just miss a century

blocks.clueFragment: Finally, they just miss a century
blocks.note: surface reading: a batsman or a person dying just short of a hundred

blocks.clueFragment: Finally, they just miss a century
blocks.note: setter's reading: the last of the two-digit numbers, such as 99, stop one short of a hundred

explanation.surface: In the end, they fall agonisingly short of a hundred runs.
explanation.walkthrough: A century is a hundred runs in cricket; 'finally' points to the top end of the two-digit numbers, which stop at 99.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers from ten to ninety-nine have two digits, and the highest of them falls just below one hundred.

clue.text: A source of continuing pride

blocks.note: surface reading: something that keeps on making someone proud
setter's reading: a pride is a group of big cats, and the female keeps it going by bearing cubs

explanation.surface: Something that gives lasting satisfaction and self-respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Pride the feeling is the false path; pride the group of big cats is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the big cat bears the cubs that keep a pride going, so she is where its future comes from.

clue.text: Someone very determined to find a plane?

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who never gives up
second meaning: a fast military aircraft built for combat

explanation.surface: A person with real resolve is needed to track down an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolute person who battles on is called this, and so is a combat jet built to attack other aircraft.

clue.text: Legal adviser briefly left out of musical wrangling

indicators.note: something left out of a group is omitted, so the abbreviation for left disappears from the word that follows
wrangling is noisy arguing, which suggests the letters are tossed about and rearranged

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left, and it is the letter dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer was briefly excluded from the arguments over a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' belongs to the definition: the answer is the short form of amicus curiae. 'Left' here is both the letter L and the sign that it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin term amicus curiae, 'friend of the court', names an impartial expert who advises judges; it is often shortened.

clue.text: Greek character facing total disaster, having mixed parentage

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the word just before it is broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek figure faces complete ruin because of a mixed family background.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is now considered offensive; it was in standard use when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The dated term, now offensive, described a person with one Black and one white parent.

clue.text: Time to pack in dodgy cigars affecting one's digestion?

indicators.note: to pack something in is to stuff it inside, so the single letter goes within the other letters
something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the word after it is twisted into a new order

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: It's time to give up dodgy cigars that upset one's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack in' looks like 'quit', but it means put inside: T goes into the rearranged CIGARS.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the stomach, the organ where food is broken down, so it concerns the digestive process.

clue.text: "River horse", so it's said

indicators.note: something that is said is spoken out, so the word before it is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a roan is a horse with a coat flecked with white

explanation.surface: A hippopotamus, which literally means river horse, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River horse' suggests the hippopotamus, but the two words are split: the river is the definition and the horse supplies the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The major European waterway flows from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean near Marseille.

clue.text: Whip pinching MP's cheese?

indicators.note: pinching grips something between two sides, so the first word's letters hold the second inside

blocks.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A party whip helps himself to a politician's cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whip looks like a parliamentary officer, matching MP, but it is the cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft, creamy, white-rinded variety from Normandy is one of the best-known French dairy products.

clue.text: Recalled section of book originally specifying hardwood

indicators.note: a section is only a part, so the letters are lifted from inside the following words
to recall is to call back, so the extracted letters are read in the backward direction

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A recalled extract from a book that first named a type of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: This durable West African tree yields a tough, teak-like timber used for furniture and boatbuilding.

clue.text: Tabloid king scuppered

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A popular-paper magnate has been ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is scuppered has been deliberately sent to the bottom, and figuratively a plan so treated is ruined.

clue.text: Precise time to phone up - very excited about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, and 'that' points back at the preceding words, which go inside

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to phone someone up is to ring them
someone who is sent is carried away with delight

explanation.surface: An exact moment to make a call, and someone thrilled about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sent, as in 'that music really sends me', is an old slang word for thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules or standards that are strict and exacting leave no room for laxity, so they are rigorously precise.
